quote: Example 3.1. Suppose X1, X2, X3 are independent random variables with Xi ∼ PGW(p, q, λi), i = 1, 2, 3, where (λ1, λ2, λ3) = (1.5, 2, 3.5). Assume that the hazard rates of X3:3 and Y3:3 are denoted, respectively, by h(.; 1.5, 2, 3.5) and h(.; λ, λ, λ). quote: Example 4.1. Suppose X1, X2, X3 are independent random variables with Xi ∼ PGW(2, 1, λi), i = 1, 2, 3, where (λ1, λ2, λ3) = (0.1, 1, 9). Further, suppose Y1, Y2, Y3 is another set of independent random variables with Yi ∼ PGW(2, 1, µi), i = 1, 2, 3, where (µ1, µ2, µ3) = (0.1, 4, 6). It is easy to observe that (λ1, λ2, λ3) ≽p (µ1, µ2, µ3). On the other hand, we have F̄X3:3(0.8)/F̄Y3:3(0.8) = 1.00339, F̄X3:3(1)/F̄Y3:3(1) = 1.0037, F̄X3:3(1.9)/F̄Y3:3(1.9) = 1.0019. Let (X1,1, ···, X1,n1, X2,1, ···, X2,n2) and (Y1,1, ···, Y1,n1, Y2,1, ···, Y2,n2) be two independent random vectors with (i) Xi,j ∼ PGW(p, q, λi) and Yi,j ∼ PGW(p, q, λ*i), j = 1,···,ni, i = 1, 2 or (ii) Xi,j ∼ GG(α, qα, λi) and Yi,j ∼ GG(α, qα, λ*i), j = 1,···,ni, i = 1, 2. Assume that λ1 ≤ λ*1 ≤ λ*2 ≤ λ2. Then, for q ≤ 1, the following three statements are equivalent: (i) (λ1,...,λ1,λ2,...,λ2) ≽p (λ*1,...,λ*1,λ*2,...,λ*2) [n1 and n2 copies]; (ii) Xn:n ≥hr Yn:n; (iii) Xn:n ≥st Yn:n.
